blocker_recorded: Default winding permutation cannot be used until explicit package binding is corrected and tested.
blocker_resolution: The WE datasheet (744272222 rev 007.000, archived sha a5e6c7bb...) p1 schematic gives windings 1->2 and 4->3 (dots at 1 and 4) in manufacturer numbering. Its top-view dimension drawing puts pins 3-4 (and so 1-2) 7.62 ±0.1 apart and pins 1-4 6.22 ±0.1 apart. The OHMNI 3D coordinates (spec line 3478: 1 (-3.81,+3.11), 2 (-3.81,-3.11), 3 (+3.81,-3.11), 4 (+3.81,+3.11)) put 7.62 between package 1-4 and 2-3, so package numbering is not manufacturer numbering. Keeping pin 1 fixed and matching the 7.62/6.22 axes gives manufacturer->package {1:1, 2:4, 3:3, 4:2}. In package numbering the windings are therefore 1-4 and 2-3 with dots at 1 and 2, which happens to equal the spec's through-flow default. That default was right only by coincidence and was never evidenced, so the binding should carry the explicit permutation through pin_role_fact rather than the default. The proposed binding is DC winding resistance only (op), so leakage, saturation and HF fit stay out.

blocker_recorded: Physical/reference and primary-conductor binding conflict; open-secondary operation is hazardous.
blocker_resolution: Kept blocked. (1) The primary is a separate conductor threaded through the aperture (entry field primary_connection, AS series doc p1). The recipe mechanism binds model roles only to package terminals, and the class template needs P1/P2, so there is no package pin to carry the primary and any P1/P2 binding would be invented. (2) Exact AS-103 non-centre-tapped has secondary pins 1 and 3 only (pin2_present = false), while the 3D package carries a pin 2, so the physical reference conflicts. (3) The class template hard-wires Rburden across S1-S2 inside the model, which would hide the open-secondary hazard (bench B3: ~236 V peak open-circuit) instead of refusing it. A secondary-only DC binding would be technically sourceable (10 ohm max DCR) but meaningless for a CT and would invite open-secondary use, so it is not proposed. The isolation figure (2500 or 4000 V AC) is not assigned to AS-103 in the series sheet.
